linkedin.hook: Composable margin on Soroban: why isolated SmartAccounts matter for Blend v2 b-token integration.
linkedin.copy:
Blend v2 published its formally verified pool architecture, clarifying how b-tokens mint and accrue interest on Stellar. While pooled lending protocols provide core money market liquidity, institutional strategies stall when position management requires multiple signature rounds across disparate contracts. Pooled risk models force conservative loan-to-value ratios because liquidation engines cannot guarantee atomic debt servicing under market stress.

Vanna addresses this by decoupling account custody from position management via isolated SmartAccount sandboxes. Instead of routing interactions through shared liquidity silos, SmartAccounts deploy deterministic contracts that borrow and deposit directly into Blend v2 b-token pools within a single transaction envelope. Relying on ~320ms Mercury indexer latency and predictable 0.00014 XLM fixed gas fees, smart accounts execute rebalances against a hard 1.10x Health Factor floor without leaving intermediate states open to frontrunning.

The result is institutional-grade capital efficiency where leverage loops are managed programmatically rather than manually babysat. Builders and risk managers can verify execution paths and audit position health on Soroban testnet today. Deploy your testnet SmartAccount sandbox at test.stellar.vanna.finance.

reddit.hook: How we route borrowed liquidity into Blend v2 b-tokens using Soroban SmartAccounts (testnet live)
reddit.copy:
The Blend team recently published their v2 pool architecture formal verification and b-token specification. It is solid work, but interacting with b-tokens as an active farmer still requires manual position management across multiple transactions. If you want to post collateral, borrow a secondary asset, wrap it into b-tokens, and loop that yield, you are typically juggling separate auth signatures and praying network latency does not spike your slippage.

We built Vanna to solve this on Soroban via isolated SmartAccounts.

### Contract Architecture and Routing

Instead of holding collateral in a global pooled contract, each user spins up a deterministic SmartAccount sandbox. The contract implements Soroban custom account abstraction, allowing batch execution in a single ledger close. When you initiate a loop, the SmartAccount borrows the base asset from the lending pool, wraps the borrowed capital into Blend v2 b-tokens, and locks the yield-bearing receipt back inside the SmartAccount as synthetic margin.

Everything resolves in one atomic transaction envelope. Gas remains fixed at roughly 0.00014 XLM, while our Mercury indexer integration gives us state updates at ~320ms latency. Because positions are isolated per sandbox, a default in an exotic collateral pool cannot bleed into other accounts.

### Risk Parameters

We set a strict 1.10x Health Factor floor for leveraged positions. If market drift pushes an account toward that threshold, liquidator bots trigger partial unwinds directly against the underlying b-token pool rather than dumping raw collateral on an AMM. This limits price impact and preserves capital for the borrower.

### Testing on Testnet

You can test the contract calls directly. Deploy your testnet SmartAccount sandbox at test.stellar.vanna.finance to run your own loops:

1. Fund a testnet account with friendbot XLM.
2. Mint testnet collateral into your sandbox.
3. Trigger the b-token routing hook to borrow and wrap in one ledger close.
4. Monitor Health Factor updates via the indexer.

Disclosure: I am a core engineer building Vanna Protocol. We are actively stress-testing our Soroban contracts against Blend v2 testnet deployments and welcome technical feedback on our execution logic.
